design_fidelity.note: Matches the design (m5-planets.md 'Apparent disc' and 'Gravity hold' sections): conformal image, centre = mean of edge images not the aberrated centre, hoverPower = m_eff |g| c. One documented deviation from the sprint plan: the plan said 'aberrate theta +- alpha with cosSeen; near-c branch uses oneMinusBeta(phi)'; the implementation uses the half-angle law tan(theta'/2) = e^-phi tan(theta/2) via atan2 instead. This is strictly better (no 1 - beta anywhere, exact at both poles, continuous and odd so a pole crossing needs no branch) and is explained in optics.ail:124-133 and the CHANGELOG. -1: the designed cosTheta input re-introduces acos conditioning at the forward pole (acos(1 - 1e-16) = 1.49e-8 rad), so the half-angle law's precision is only fully available when the caller has theta; an angle-input overload (angleSeen is exported, so callers can compose it) would close that. Sub-pixel in the game, so a remark not a defect.

independent_physics.method: Own oracle (scratchpad my_disc_oracle.py): 3,600 rim points of the rest-frame circle built in 3D, each Lorentz-transformed with the 4-vector law (transverse / gamma(1 + beta cos theta), longitudinal (cos theta + beta)/(1 + beta cos theta)) in float64, image fitted by min/max polar angle and checked circular; no half-angle law anywhere. Pole-crossing rows re-done in 60-digit Decimal (scratchpad polecross3d.py) because a min/max-polar-angle fit is wrong when the pole is inside the image.
independent_physics.conformal: Image of the rim is a circle: max deviation 7.4e-15 rad (RS-24/25), 2.7e-14 (RS-26/27), 5.1e-15 (RS-28/29), 1.7e-15 (beta 0.5), 2.7e-12 at the cap (float64 Lorentz arithmetic at gamma 707); 60-digit: 1e-58 to 3e-55 rad for all rows including pole crossings. Aberration is a Mobius map of the sphere, so this is expected and the package relies on it correctly.
independent_physics.RS-24/25: beta 0.9, theta 90, alpha 5: my centre 25.9277296298034, radius 2.1839405633943, aberrated centre 25.8419327631671 deg; vs package 1.1e-14 / 5.3e-15 deg (4e-16 / 2.4e-15 relative). The 0.0858 deg centre offset from the aberrated centre is real (rim at psi=0 appears at 28.1117, psi=180 at 23.7438 deg).
independent_physics.RS-28/29: beta 0.9, theta 150: 82.0207127068368 / 9.9404108106039 deg; vs package 0 / 3.6e-16 relative. Magnified astern (9.94 > 5), as the design says.
independent_physics.cap_row: 1 - beta = 1e-6, theta 90, alpha 5: 0.0813379904048 / 0.0070890706043 deg; vs package 2.0e-11 relative, which is my float64 method's conditioning at gamma 707, not the package's (the package's test tolerance 1e-11 against the 60-digit oracle holds).
independent_physics.D_at_apparent_centre: 1/(gamma(1 - beta cos c')) at my centres: 2.287075180161, 7.062324486291, 0.498122075824; vs package 0 / 1.8e-15 / 3.3e-16 relative. Confirms the convention D = 1/(gamma(1 - beta cos theta')) with theta' the apparent angle, as spec section 2 and dopplerApparent (optics.ail:53-58) use.
independent_physics.half_angle_law_vs_cosSeen: cos(2 atan2(e^-phi sin(theta/2), cos(theta/2))) vs (cos theta + beta)/(1 + beta cos theta) over 1e4 random (theta, beta<0.999999): worst |dcos| 1.35e-14. Same convention (sources crowd forward), same sign of phi.
independent_physics.pole_crossing: theta 2, alpha 5, 0.9c: package centre 0.45970446280509 radius 1.14810066536588 deg, 60-digit truth 0.459704462805109 / 1.148100665365885; pole 0.4597 deg from the image centre < radius, so the forward pole stays inside. theta 178, alpha 5: 171.58372056888393 / 21.439602329101284 vs truth 171.583720568883668 / 21.439602329101303; astern pole 8.42 deg from centre < 21.44 radius, inside. theta 0.5 alpha 1 and theta 179.5 alpha 1 at the cap also inside. The signed nearEdge = angleSeen(theta - alpha) with theta - alpha < 0 (angleSeen odd) is exactly right; clamping or mirroring it is wrong (mutations M4-M6).
independent_physics.precision_near_poles: theta 1e-6 rad at the cap: half-angle law 2.9e-16 relative error, acos(cosSeen) returns 0.0 (100% error). theta 1e-4 at the cap: 3.7e-16 vs 1.1e-2. theta pi - 1e-6 at the cap: 1.1e-14 vs 2.0e-8. theta 1e-3 at 0.9c: 0 vs 5.9e-10. angleSeen(pi/2, cap) = 1.4142136802e-3 rad (= 2 atan(e^-phi), finite). The AGENT.md claim is correct.
independent_physics.angleSeen_symmetries: angleSeen(-0.5) + angleSeen(0.5) = 0.0 exactly; angleSeen(2pi - 1) + angleSeen(1) = 6.283185307179586 (= 2pi); angleSeen(pi) = 3.1415926535897927 (1 ulp below pi, from h = pi/2 giving cos(h) = 6.1e-17). Oddness and the 2pi mirror hold as documented.
independent_physics.NaN: apparentDisc(NaN, 0.1, phi) -> {NaN, NaN}; hoverPower(1, NaN) -> NaN. Propagates, no trap. Not folded into discDigest (suggest adding one NaN row, since the ensures clauses compare NaN and ailang#1419 makes NaN >= x engine-dependent if contracts are ever enforced at runtime).
independent_physics.hoverPower: HB-90: P_hover = m_eff a_hover c with a_hover = GM/(r^2 sqrt(1 - r_s/r)) (higgs-bubble.md lines 351-367). Package test rebuilds HB-88 4.82e5 m/s^2 and HB-90 1.44e14 W/kg from HB-10 (4.297e6 M_sun, IAU GM_sun) at 3 r_s; optics_ref.py gives 4.81891152459916e5 and 1.44467333084411e14, matching the spec's printed digits. hoverPower(1, 0.1254) = 37593974.233200006 W = 0.1254 c. Meaning: the bubble's own acceleration is unfelt (property 3), so the drive must supply F = m_eff |g| as photon thrust; a collimated photon exhaust carries momentum E/c, so F = P/c and P = F c = m_eff |g| c. Consistent with medium.photonDriveEnergy's model and with the design's 'about 3.8e7 W per kg of m_eff' at 0.125 m/s^2. The |g| fold is right: hovering against g in either sign costs the same.
